metadata.name: DurableDirectory
metadata.description: Persistent storage on disk: a writable directory whose files survive restarts, reloads, redeployments and new versions of the application, for as long as whoever runs it keeps the storage. Asks for a minimum size and for single-writer or shared access; the directory is empty the first time and is no backup.

path.description: The directory, an absolute path the application can write to. It exists and is writable before any resource initializes; a full directory is reported by the operating system's own error (`ENOSPC`).

size.description: The least space the application needs: a whole number followed by `Mi`, `Gi` or `Ti` (`512Mi`, `5Gi`, `1Ti`). A host may give more, and may refuse a size it cannot give; nothing measures it.

access.description: `single-writer`: at most one running instance of the application has the directory at any moment, a rollout or a restart included, and the application may rely on that. `shared`: every instance has it at once, on different machines; file locking across them is not reliable, so the application coordinates its own writes, and SQLite is not safe there.
